transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-02
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Sam Cortez (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (BrightPath Eng Mgr), Maya Patel (BrightPath ML Lead), Rafael Ortega (BrightPath Infra)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I can see folks. Priya, Sam, you on?
[00:06] Priya (SE): Yep here. Hi all.
[00:08] Sam (CSM): Sam here. Good afternoon.
[00:12] Jordan (Eng Mgr): Jordan here for BrightPath.
[00:14] Maya (ML Lead): Maya here.
[00:16] Rafael (Infra): Rafael joining from infra.
[00:18] Alex: Awesome. Agenda today: gate review for onboarding, creds and VPC peering status, we want to hand off a short latency script, and confirm next steps for dedicated sizing.
[00:28] Jordan: Sounds good. We've got a few blockers from our side around the service account and our firewall rules.
[00:33] Priya: Got it — we'll aim to make the creds handoff as low-friction as possible. Rafael, have you got the list of required egress rules we sent earlier?
[00:41] Rafael: I pulled those but haven't pushed them live yet. We need to confirm the IP ranges. I was hoping Redwood could provide the ephemeral ranges or a service CIDR so security can approve.
[00:51] Alex: Yes, we can provide either ephemeral / region ranges or a FQDN-based egress list. For the POC we usually give a short list of IPs and region endpoints. I'll share the CIDR block in the notes after the call.
[01:02] Maya: One question — for the latency tests, do you want us to use the production prompt families or smaller toy prompts?
[01:09] Priya: Please use representative prompts — ideally the two families you said you care about: long-context summarization and short in-line rewrite. The profiler we send will accept both.
[01:18] Jordan: Understood. Rafael, can infra set up a test runner in our staging VPC?
[01:22] Rafael: Yes. I can spin up a small runner, but we need the service account creds and an example config.
[01:28] Alex: We'll provision a scoped service account with minimal permissions — token-based auth for the pilot, not full keys. We'll include rotation instructions.
[01:36] Sam: Quick note: for customers doing VPC peering there may be a short window where we need to open ports for health checks — we'll note that in the egress doc.
[01:45] Rafael: That helps. Also, KMS — do you support customer-managed keys for logs and model payloads in the POC?
[01:53] Priya: We do support KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private. For hosted POC we can show how envelope encryption works; customer-managed keys require a Private or Dedicated arrangement with a KMS connector. We'll add the architecture diagram to the drive.
[02:06] Jordan: Cool. I want to be explicit about success criteria: 1) ability to call the API from staging with <150ms median generation for short prompts 2) consistent output quality for the sample prompts, and 3) no data exfiltration concerns in our audit logs.
[02:19] Alex: Love that — measurable and clear. We'll run the latency baseline and provide token-level cost estimates for each prompt family.
[02:26] Maya: For quality checking, we'll share gold responses for 8-10 prompts. I want to make sure quantization or batching doesn't regress our paraphrase fidelity.
[02:36] Priya: Noted — we'll keep the model quantization conservative for these tests. If you want to see quantized variants we can run a side-by-side.
[02:44] Jordan: Question on KV cache — does Redwood's runtime maintain per-session KV cache and will that be included in the POC? We rely heavily on prefix caching for session bots.
[02:54] Priya: Yes, the runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; for the POC we'll enable the cache but keep TTLs short. Warning — profiling sometimes underreports if cache warmup isn't simulated. We'll provide a script to sequence requests so you can see warm/cold behavior.
[03:11] Alex: I'll drop the profiler link in chat — it's a small python script that runs multiple sequences and emits latency percentiles and KV hit rates.
[03:18] Rafael: Please include instructions for both NAT and private link scenarios since our staging sometimes uses NAT gateways.
[03:24] Priya: Absolutely. The README will show options for NAT egress and for private link / VPC endpoint.
[03:29] Jordan: On dedicated capacity — we need a cost estimate for a small reserved pool (two GPUs-ish) and what's the expected latency SLO.
[03:36] Alex: For a two-GPU reserved pool, typical median latencies for short prompts are in the 80–130ms range depending on model family. I'll send a sizing + cost table with conservative throughput targets.
[03:47] Jordan: Are there any known perf regressions when you enable batch merging? Our throughput pattern is bursty, so batching may increase latency tail.
[03:55] Priya: Good callout. Our runtime uses continuous batching with policies; we can tune the max wait window and adaptive batching thresholds. For POC we'll leave batching conservative to prioritize tail latency. We'll show two runs: low-latency config and cost-optimized config so you can compare.
[04:15] Maya: That would be helpful. Also, can Redwood instrument token-level cost breakdown per request? We want to map to our product metrics.
[04:22] Alex: Yes, the console exposes token count and cost per route; we'll include an example CSV export in the report.
[04:29] Rafael: About SSO — we use SAML at BrightPath. For Private deployments do you do SAML SSO or only OIDC?
[04:36] Priya: Both. Private supports SAML and OIDC; hosted supports OIDC primarily but we can bring SAML integrations through enterprise setups. We'll send the SSO integration doc.
[04:45] Jordan: Great. Anything on the legal front — do you have a standard pilot DPA or data processing notes?
[04:52] Alex: We have a pilot addendum and a DPA we can attach. For the POC we typically include a data handling section clarifying log retention and who manages keys. I'll attach those to the Drive folder.
[05:03] Sam: Quick administrative note: I'll create the shared Drive folder and invite everyone — put logs, profiler, egress rules there.
[05:09] Rafael: Perfect. Please include a README so security can find the relevant docs quickly.
[05:13] Alex: Will do.
[05:15] [06:00] (short silence while folks check links)
[06:10] Maya: Rafael and I will pick two representative prompt families this week and upload gold outputs.
[06:16] Rafael: Yes, target by next Monday.
[06:18] Jordan: Rafael — can you confirm network gating will be handled by 2025-09-03? Our security change window is limited.
[06:25] Rafael: I'll aim for it; I need the CIDR from Redwood and I'll open the ticket today.
[06:29] Alex: I'll publish the CIDR and the ephemeral IP list to the Drive in the next hour.
[06:33] Priya: On the profiling script — small notes: it simulates cache warm-up, then runs a short burst pattern to approximate your traffic. It outputs p50/p90/p99 and KV hit-rate. Rafael, that should map to your runner.
[06:45] Rafael: Sounds good. Is the script synchronous calls only? We usually run async runners.
[06:49] Priya: It's sync by default but there's an async mode; we'll include both.
[06:53] Jordan: Any blockers from Redwood side for the handoff?
[06:56] Alex: No blockers. We need the service account approval. Once Rafael confirms the peering ticket, we provision the scoped credentials.
[07:04] Maya: For the quality check — if we see a regression with quantized models, what's the rollback path?
[07:10] Priya: We'll pin model versions for the POC and we can disable quantization on the fly. If you prefer, we can run everything on non-quantized for the first run.
[07:18] Alex: We should agree on the initial model variant — suggest starting with the verified open model in our catalog that matches your latency/quality tradeoff. We'll list alternatives.
[07:26] Jordan: Ok. Also, can we capture traces for a few requests to debug tokenization mismatch?
[07:31] Priya: Yes, the console supports request tracing for selected calls; we'll show how to enable sampling.
[07:36] Rafael: On log retention — our compliance policy wants 90 days of access logs. Is that feasible?
[07:42] Sam: Our default retention is 30 days for the pilot, but for enterprise we can extend. We'll flag this for compliance and include retention extension options in the security doc.
[07:52] Jordan: Thanks.
[07:54] Alex: Quick recap / next steps: Redwood provision service account + CIDR (Alex) by 2025-09-03; Priya to upload profiler and README by 2025-09-04; Rafael to validate VPC peering and open firewall ticket by 2025-09-03; Maya to upload gold prompts by 2025-09-08; schedule dedicated sizing call for 2025-09-05. Anything to add?
[08:15] Jordan: That covers it.
[08:17] Rafael: Fine with me.
[08:19] Maya: Good.
[08:21] Alex: We'll follow up with calendar invites. Sam will own the Drive folder.
[08:25] Sam: I'll create the folder and drop the initial assets and invite the group.
[08:28] [41:30] (meeting ends)

Notes & links referenced:
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-redwood-brightpath (placeholder)
- Profiler script: /drive/profiler/latency_profiler_v1.py (attached in Drive)
- Security deck: /drive/security/soc2_kms_sso.pdf
- Dedicated sizing spreadsheet: /drive/pricing/dedicated_sizing.xlsx

Transcript quirks: occasional mistranscription ("K V cash" instead of "KV cache", "ded-acted" heard once for "Dedicated"), filler words, and overlapping talk captured as separate speaker labels in a couple spots.

Final recap (verbal):
- Redwood will hand off scoped service account + CIDR for egress by 2025-09-03.
- BrightPath will run profiler and share results; Redwood will review and propose tuned configs.
- Dedicated sizing call set for 2025-09-05 to finalize reserve options.

End of transcript.
